_standing: TRANSFER CARD — a pipeline demonstration on a second case, not a finding for the proband. No allele in any person is asserted. Built 2026-09-19 from a second mosaic-variegated-aneuploidy gene with a different disease, a different tumour and its own public phenotype annotation: TRIP13 causes MVA3 (OMIM 617598, MONDO:0054736) and the reported malignancy is nephroblastoma in 6 of 6 annotated cases, not rhabdomyosarcoma. It shares the spindle assembly checkpoint with the template case, so a transfer that works is a statement about the pipeline rather than about how unlike the two cases are - and it shares no disease query, no clinical term list, no tumour context and no standard-of-care drug with it, with the template card's case-agnostic blocks (anti-directions, evidence ladder, constraints) copied from the BUB1B card version 5. Only the automated rungs apply: this card has no curated evidence.tsv.

gene.protein: Pachytene checkpoint protein 2 homolog (TRIP13, thyroid hormone receptor interactor 13); an AAA+ ATPase
gene._verified: UniProt REST Q15645 on 2026-09-20: recommended name 'Pachytene checkpoint protein 2 homolog', gene TRIP13, Ensembl ENSG00000071539. HGNC REST symbol/TRIP13: HGNC:12307, uniprot_ids ['Q15645']

mechanism.class: loss-of-function, biallelic (public literature; this card asserts no variant in any person)
mechanism.status: demonstration only: the transfer card exists to run the pipeline on a second case, not to diagnose anyone. The mechanism below is what the cited literature states about TRIP13-related MVA3
mechanism.pathway: spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) - MAD2 conformational switching and mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC) disassembly by the TRIP13 AAA+ ATPase with p31comet (MAD2L1BP)
mechanism.immediate_effect: loss of TRIP13 ATPase activity leaves MAD2 stuck in its closed, checkpoint-active conformation and the MCC undisassembled; the checkpoint cannot be silenced or reset, and error correction at the kinetochore fails
downstream: mosaic variegated aneuploidy (different chromosomes in different cells)
cancer predisposition, with nephroblastoma (Wilms tumour) the reported malignancy

literature.role: Yost 2017 (Nat Genet): biallelic TRIP13 mutations predispose to Wilms tumor and chromosome missegregation - the MVA3 disease definition and the tumour context
Eytan 2015 (PNAS): mode of interaction of the TRIP13 AAA-ATPase with the Mad2-binding protein p31comet and with mitotic checkpoint complexes - the D3 axis
2017 (Nat Commun): mechanistic insight into TRIP13-catalyzed Mad2 structural transition and spindle checkpoint silencing

repurposing_directions.name: SAC reinforcement / chromosomal-instability reduction
repurposing_directions.rationale: the same direction the template card asks, on this case's checkpoint: agents that prolong mitotic checkpoint arrest or stabilise kinetochore-microtubule attachments. Seeds are the checkpoint core plus TRIP13 and its partner p31comet (MAD2L1BP)

repurposing_directions.name: aneuploidy-selective stress exploitation
repurposing_directions.rationale: aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic and energy stress whatever caused the aneuploidy, so this direction's seed set is the case-agnostic one: AMPK energy stress, the HSP90/HSF1 chaperone axis, autophagy and the proteasome, and the TFEB lysosomal response. Caveat carried over unchanged: this kills aneuploid cells, so it is a tumour-context and chemoprevention angle, not a treatment of the constitutional mosaic state

repurposing_directions.name: TRIP13 / p31comet proteostasis axis
repurposing_directions.rationale: this case's own mechanism direction, and the one that differs most from the template's: TRIP13 is an AAA+ ATPase that, with p31comet (MAD2L1BP), extracts MAD2 from the mitotic checkpoint complex (PMID 26324890, 29208896). A loss-of-function AAA+ ATPase is a protein-remodelling problem, so the seeds are the axis itself plus the drugged arms of cellular proteostasis - the related AAA+ ATPase VCP, the proteasome, and the HSP90/HSP70 chaperones

repurposing_directions.name: cancer surveillance in the nephroblastoma context
repurposing_directions.rationale: the reported malignancy of this case is nephroblastoma, so this is the tumour-context direction and the only one the automated rungs 4 and 5 apply to. Seeds are the genes the Wilms tumour literature drugs or targets: the WT1/IGF2 developmental axis, WNT/beta-catenin, TP53, mTOR and VEGFA

anti_directions.name: further checkpoint weakening
anti_directions.agents: Mps1/TTK inhibitors, Aurora B inhibitors, MAD2/BUB1 inhibition - none market-approved
anti_directions.why: aneuploid cancer cells are selectively killed by mitotic checkpoint inhibition (PMID 33505028) - the same logic makes a constitutionally SAC-deficient child the worst candidate for it; mitotic slippage is the failure mode (PMID 30601084)

anti_directions.name: spindle poisons in a SAC-deficient background
anti_directions.agents: vinca alkaloids and taxanes - standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy
anti_directions.why: spindle poisons rely on a working checkpoint to arrest cells; MVA1 cells have a weakened checkpoint (PMID 20516114) and slip through mitosis (PMID 30601084). Flagged for the treating team as a hypothesis to weigh, never as advice to withhold standard therapy

evidence_ladder.purpose: every candidate drug is placed on one rung before it is argued; rung 1 is named, never submitted

rungs.label: approved for a related indication, with paediatric use
rungs.test: an approved drug with an openFDA label carrying a pediatric_use section or a ClinicalTrials.gov study in the tumour context that admits children

rungs.label: clinical trial in a related indication
rungs.test: a registered study of the drug in the disease or the tumour context

rungs.label: in-vivo model of aneuploidy or checkpoint deficiency
rungs.test: a cited animal result on the direction's mechanism (a PMID in evidence.tsv)

rungs.label: cell model in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cells
rungs.test: a cited cellular result on the direction's mechanism (a PMID in evidence.tsv)

rungs.label: mechanism only
rungs.test: the drug acts on a target in the direction's set and nothing above applies

evidence_ladder.rule: the rung is the highest test the drug passes; automated tests (approval, label, trials) and curated tests (a PMID read by a person) are printed side by side and never merged silently; a curated row may carry proxy=true when the cited result is for a same-axis compound rather than the approved molecule itself; the automated rungs 4 and 5 rest on a trial in the tumour context and therefore apply only to a direction marked context=true (the tumour-context direction) - a rhabdomyosarcoma trial says nothing about a checkpoint or proteostasis mechanism (refinement recorded in methodology 113 after the first grading run)

constraints.eligibility: market-approved drugs only (challenge rules, Track 2 definition); ChEMBL max_phase 4 or an FDA label is the evidence of approval
